summary: Same Enchantments in an item components crashes the game
description: when you have 2 enchantments "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" in the new components this will crash the game 1./give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}] 2./give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}] the second one will crash the game, but the first one doesnt.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open a world where you have permission to use commands.  
2. Run the command ``/give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}]``.  
3. Observe that the command completes and the sword is received without the game crashing.  
4. Run the command ``/give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}]``.  
5. Wait a moment for the command to process.  
6. Observe that the game crashes after executing the second command.
Observed Behavior: When the command /give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}] is executed the game immediately crashes, both the client and any integrated server close and the world cannot be re‑opened, while using /give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}] does not cause a crash and the sword appears with Sharpness 10 as expected; the crash is reproducible on the latest Java 1.21 snapshot, occurs on a fresh world with no other modifications, and the crash report shows a NullPointerException originating from the item‑component handling code when the enchantments component contains two entries that resolve to the same enchantment but are stored under different keys – one using the short identifier “sharpness” and the other using the fully‑qualified identifier “minecraft:sharpness”. The game attempts to merge the duplicate enchantments during component deserialization, encounters an unexpected duplicate key situation, and aborts execution, resulting in the observed loss of the session.
Expected Behavior: When a diamond sword is given with an enchantments component that lists the same enchantment twice—once as the short name “sharpness” and once as the fully‑qualified name “minecraft:sharpness”—the game should treat them as a single enchantment, apply the highest specified level, and create the item without error. No crash or instability should occur regardless of which identifier is used.
